articles.title: No Flag Does Not Mean Safe: Five Things That Went Wrong Building a Shared Medicine Record on FalkorDB
articles.excerpt: Our app once let two carers both record the same 9 pm tablet as given. One typed 21:00, the other typed 21:15, and the app saw two different doses. That bug is the reason this post exists. I built Car…
articles.body: Our app once let two carers both record the same 9 pm tablet as given. One typed 21:00, the other typed 21:15, and the app saw two different doses. That bug is the reason this post exists. I built Care Circle for Graph Hacks 2026 (Track 02, agent memory and coordination). It is a shared medicine record for families who look after one person together. This post is about five things that went wrong while building it, and what each one taught me. They look unrelated. Four of them are the same mistake. No flag is not the same as safe. When the data has a hole, the code must say so. If it fills the hole with something that looks fine, the hole becomes an answer. The problem It is 9 pm. Ravi changes his mother's warfarin dose by phone.

articles.title: RepCheck: An AI Helper That Watches Workout Videos for Online Coaches (MediaPipe + Gemma)
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle RepCheck is a helper for online personal trainers. Online coaches get workout videos from their clients every da…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built RepCheck is a helper for online personal trainers. Online coaches get workout videos from their clients every day. Watching each one closely takes hours, so feedback often ends up as just "looks good 👍". The client doesn't improve, and the coach burns out. RepCheck fixes that in four simple steps: Film it. The client films one set on their phone and uploads it. We measure it. MediaPipe finds the body in every frame. Python code counts each rep and measures depth, speed, tempo and left/right balance. We check it. Clear, fixed rules turn those numbers into a 0–100 form score and one or two simple tips.

articles.title: CODEOWNERS Is a Lie. I Built a Graph to Prove It.
articles.excerpt: Every code repository has a file that says who owns each part of the code. Nobody fully trusts that file, and there’s a good reason. People change teams. People leave projects. The file never updates…
articles.body: Every code repository has a file that says who owns each part of the code. Nobody fully trusts that file, and there’s a good reason. People change teams. People leave projects. The file never updates itself when that happens. I wanted to know how wrong that file actually is, and whether a graph database could measure the gap instead of just storing data. The setup I took every pull request merged into Home Assistant’s core repository over 180 days. About 10,000 pull requests, 1,600 modules, 1,500 contributors. I loaded all of it into FalkorDB: people, modules, pull requests, and decisions as nodes. The connections between them (who wrote what, who reviewed what, which modules depend on which, and who’s listed as the owner) became edges.

articles.title: Your pipeline failed but your YAML was fine: how a Gitaly timeout broke GitLab CI on Friday
articles.excerpt: Your pipeline failed but your YAML was fine: how a Gitaly timeout broke GitLab CI on Friday Friday afternoon. You push a commit, the pipeline kicks off, and instead of green checks you get this: "CI c…
articles.body: Your pipeline failed but your YAML was fine: how a Gitaly timeout broke GitLab CI on Friday Friday afternoon. You push a commit, the pipeline kicks off, and instead of green checks you get this: "CI configuration fetch from Gitaly timed out. This may indicate Gitaly service slowness or an outage." Your first instinct is to open your .gitlab-ci.yml and hunt for the typo. Stop. There is no typo. Your config was never read at all. What actually happened On October 16, GitLab.com had a rough afternoon. At 11:33 AM UTC, GitLab posted that CI/CD was failing for some customers with exactly that error, and that the UI was slow too. They applied a temporary mitigation at 12:28 PM UTC and marked it resolved at 1:21 PM UTC. One hour and forty-eight minutes.

articles.body: Originally published at GeekCoding101 . Why Everyone Suddenly Talks About MCP If you have used Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code Copilot lately, you have probably seen a settings page called MCP servers . People plug in an MCP server for GitHub, one for Postgres, one for their browser, one for Ghidra... and suddenly the AI can do things instead of just talking about them. In my Agentic Frameworks guide I compared the frameworks you use to build agents. MCP sits one layer below them: it is the standard plug that lets any agent or AI app talk to any tool. In this post I'll explain what an MCP server is, how it works under the hood, and then we'll build, test and connect a real one in about 60 lines of Python. 🚀 What Is MCP?

articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Sonified: Eagle Nebula Pillars Explanation: Yes, but have you ever experienced the Eagle Nebula with your ears ? The famous nebula M16 is best known for the feast it gives your eyes, highlighting bright young stars forming deep inside dark towering structures . These light-years long columns of cold gas and dust are some 6,500 light-years distant toward the constellation of the Serpent ( Serpens ).

articles.body: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk gestures as he speaks during the inaugural parade inside Capitol One Arena, in Washington, DC, on January 20, 2025. (Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP) (Photo by ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Just ahead of the wider release of Alex Gibney's Musk documentary, TikTok has banned the film's social media account from its platform. TikTok did not immediately respond to a request for comment. According to The Hollywood Reporter , the film's distributor, Bleecker Street, was informed Friday afternoon that a "permanent suspension" was imminent. Bleecker Street has not yet responded to a request for comment from The Verge .

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
